_comment: Source-of-truth mapping for Cloudflare AI Gateway dynamic-route model tiers. Apps call a TIER name via model:"dynamic/<tier>", never a raw model id. Each tier is a primary model with automatic failover to a second provider. No API key is ever sent in a request — runtime auth is the cf-aig-authorization header only.
_warning_byok_is_not_free: Storing a provider key as gateway BYOK moves that spend from Cloudflare unified credits onto YOUR provider account. It does NOT grant you the provider's free tier. For Google AI Studio specifically: if the key's Google Cloud project has billing enabled, the key is on the PAID tier and free-tier quota does not apply at all — a stored key bills full price with no 429 to warn you. Verify with `gcloud billing projects describe <project>` (or the Cloud Billing API) BEFORE treating any BYOK step as free. Do not rely on the gateway's `cost` field to catch this: it is a list-price estimate that ignores hidden reasoning tokens and undercounted real output by ~8x in our measurements.
gateway_notes: authentication=true AND store_id shared with the account's default gateway are both required. That store binding is what enables keyless Unified Billing on a NON-default gateway. Read your default gateway's store_id from GET /accounts/{account_id}/ai-gateway/gateways/default and reuse the value here.

primary.billing: BYOK — bills YOUR provider account at PAID rates unless you have verified otherwise; see _warning_byok_is_not_free

code.purpose: OPTIONAL third tier — top-end code/agentic work, quality over cost

notes.azure: Azure OpenAI CANNOT be a route step. The dynamic-route model element has no field for Azure's resource name / api-version, so an azure-openai step never reaches the provider. Re-verified 2026-07-30: such a route returns 200 but is ALWAYS answered by the fallback, and the Azure step produces NO gateway log entry at all. Storing an azure-openai BYOK secret does not fix it. The failure is graceful — outputs.fallback fires normally — so an Azure step is harmless, just useless. Consequence: an 'Azure-first / cheapest-credits-first' policy cannot be expressed as a dynamic route; it has to live in app code.
notes.invoking_dynamic_routes: dynamic/<tier> resolves ONLY on the gateway that owns the route. Pointing your base URL at a different gateway (e.g. 'default') returns HTTP 400 internalCode 2005 'Failed to get response from provider' with NO log entry — which is indistinguishable from a genuinely broken tier and will send you debugging the wrong thing. Always invoke at {gateway_base_url}/compat/chat/completions for the gateway that holds the routes.
notes.code_tier: The `code` tier deliberately falls back to a second model from the SAME provider — no cross-provider top-end code model was verified equivalent. Reduced provider diversity is an accepted trade-off there.
notes.tier_count: Two tiers (low + high) cover essentially every user-facing app path. Add `code` only if you genuinely need frontier reasoning in production.

verification.failover_proof: A throwaway route with a deliberately bogus primary model fell back to the secondary and returned HTTP 200, while a bad-only control route (no fallback) errored. Route deleted after the test. Reproduce with scripts/test-routing.sh.
verification._what_this_is: COMPATIBILITY PROBE, NOT A RECOMMENDED-MODEL LIST. Records which ids returned 200 through the compat endpoint on the date in the key name. Do NOT pick a fallback model because it appears here — ids age fast and this is not curated for quality. Check the date, then re-probe before choosing.
verification.route_step_model_constraint: Route steps MUST accept `max_tokens`. Verified 2026-07-30: every gpt-5.x model (gpt-5.4, gpt-5.1, gpt-5-mini) returns HTTP 400 "Unsupported parameter: 'max_tokens' is not supported with this model" — they require max_completion_tokens, which the compat endpoint does not translate. So a newer model is not automatically a usable fallback; this is a wire-format constraint, not a quality judgement.

compat_probe._what_this_is: A COMPATIBILITY PROBE, NOT A RECOMMENDED-MODEL LIST. It records which model ids returned 200 through the compat endpoint when last run. Do NOT pick a fallback because it appears here — model ids age fast and this is not curated for quality. Re-probe before choosing.
